Goal: I can construct medians and altitudes and locate their points of concurrence.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A median joins a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. The medians meet at the centroid G, two thirds of the way from each vertex to the opposite midpoint. G is the balance point of a cardboard triangle.

The altitudes (or the lines containing them) meet at the orthocenter H.

Euler line: in any triangle that is not equilateral, the circumcenter O, the centroid G and the orthocenter H lie on one line, with HG = 2 GO. The incenter is generally not on it.

slides.title: Try it
slides.html:
Build all four centers and discover that the circumcenter, centroid, and orthocenter lie on the Euler line (the incenter generally does not).

Use the controls in the panel. Drag the hollow points on the board.

slides.html: A median is 12 cm long. How far is the centroid from the vertex? From the midpoint?
